title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 12
paragraphs: They, then, were hurrying toward the Isthmus; and the Argives, as soon as they heard that Pausanias had gone out from Sparta with his army, sent as a herald to Attica the best long-distance runner they could find — because previously, on their own initiative, they had undertaken to Mardonius to stop the Spartans from going forth. When the herald came to Athens, he spoke as follows: “Mardonius, the Argives sent me to tell you that the young men have gone out from Lacedaemon, and the Argives are not able to stop them. With this in mind, may it be your good fortune to take measures well.”
